title: Analyzing research trends in domestic and international ‘Edtech’ using text mining
abstract: Objectives This study analyzed domestic and foreign ‘edtech’ related papers to find out what research topics researchers have been focusing on and to compare domestic and foreign research trends. Methods For this purpose, domestic papers were collected by searching for Edtech as a keyword in the Korea Citation Index (KCI), and international papers were collected by searching for Edtech as a keyword in Scopus. A total of 368 domestic and 279 international articles were collected, and the collected data was refined by zooming on titles, keywords, and abstracts. TF and TF-IDF were analyzed based on author keywords, and LDA topic modeling was performed based on abstracts, and visualized through LDAvis. Results First, the TF and TF-IDF results showed that the common author keywords selected by the authors of domestic and foreign studies were ‘digital’, ‘online’, ‘AI’, ‘COVID-19’, and ‘data’. Second, specific technologies such as ‘AI’, ‘metaverse’, and ‘virtual reality’ were the focus of domestic studies, while foreign studies focused on the broader concept of ‘technology’. Third, the topic modeling resulted in the topics of ‘artificial intelligence and data’, ‘future education and edtech’, ‘utilization and research of edtech’, and ‘changes in teaching before and after COVID’ in domestic studies, and ‘changes and research of edtech’, ‘student-centered learning and design’, ‘educational innovation using data and technology’, and ‘edtech from a business perspective’ in international studies. Conclusions The TF, TF-IDF, and topic modeling analysis of author keywords showed more similarities and contexts between domestic and international studies than differences. These results were similar to previous studies such as Kimmons et al. (2021), Kimmons, & Rosenberg (2022), and Allman (2023), which analyzed trends and trends in educational technology. The research on edtech is not only focused on academic research trends, but online and digital have been consistently emphasized in the global education scene. Future research on edtech needs to be conducted on various topics such as markets, industries, and comparative analysis by country.

title: Exploring Healthcare Research Patterns in Developed and Developing Countries: ATopic Modeling Perspectives
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
        <jats:p>Healthcare research has become an integral part of shaping medical improvements due to its importance in discovering health challenges, examining public health concerns, and providing evidence-based practices. Regarding the differences that exist among nations concerning their culture, infrastructure, and politics, the study of healthcare research specific to each country provides valuable lessons for policymaking and reforms based on the needs of that nation. Moreover, if there are common concerns between different countries, it can facilitate scientific cooperation. Accordingly, the purpose of this current study is to provide a cross-country overview of research themes and sub-themes on healthcare in four countries: China, England, and Iran. A total of 5122 Scopus-indexed publications related to healthcare from 2010 to 2023 are analyzed using state-of-the-art topic modeling techniques: Latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA), Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF), and BERTopic. Comparing the topic models based on evaluation metrics, BERTopic was outperformed and selected for further analysis. The results give insights into the most prevalent themes and sub-themes on healthcare in each country. Additionally, the study shows the evolution trends of the predominant topics identified for each country, showing their rise, fall, and fluctuation patterns within the literature. The findings of this study can provide helpful insight for both academics and policymakers to develop their efforts and make better decisions in this field.</jats:p>
author: Mahmoudi Laya;Sharifi Mohammad Hossein;Bagheri Ruhollah;berahmand kamal;

title: A Study of Air Quality Modeling Based on Transportation Sources through Bibliometric Analysis
abstract:
Abstract

Air quality models refer to mathematical representations or computer simulations of the distribution and changes in the concentration of air pollutants in specific areas or locations over time. The aim of this research is to map the current global state of research and future development trends in air quality modeling studies based on transportation sources. The results of this mapping will serve as a foundation for identifying research novelty in the topic of air pollutant dispersion models from transportation sources. This study employs a bibliometric approach by analyzing 1,122 scientific publications over half a century using the Scopus database. The findings indicate that Atmospheric Environment and the United States are the most productive publication sources and country, respectively, in the field of air quality modeling from the transportation sector. The mapping results using VOS viewer version 1.6.19 show that out of 8,590 keywords, 371 keywords were considered to meet the criteria. The clustering results show the interconnection between keywords. The more connected a keyword is, the more research has been conducted on that keyword. The mapping results indicate that several computational air quality models can be further developed for research purposes. These computational models include AERMOD, CALINE4, WRF-Chem, and CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics). These computing models have their respective advantages and disadvantages. In summary, further research is needed to develop simpler yet computationally efficient air quality models that integrate atmospheric chemical reactions and obstacle factors while maintaining high accuracy.
author: Eko Handriyono, Rachmanu;Hermana, Joni;Fadli Assomadi, Abdu;

title: An Analysis of Smart Logistics Trend using LDA Topic Modeling
abstract: This study aims to identify smart logistics trends, the trend of using cutting-edge technologies, and find actual and potential problems and issues in smart logistics focusing on examples from representative e-commerce companies in Korea, the USA, and China. To achieve this purpose, we collected 3,402 papers from Scopus, published between January 2001 and February 2024, and conducted Word Frequency, TF-IDF and LDA Topic Modeling analyses using Python 3. As a result of the study, five topics related to current trends and problems of smart logistics were identified: 'Un-tact services for customer convenience,' 'IoT-based technologies,' 'Development of Optimal Logistics Paths,' 'Technologies used in last-mile delivery,' and 'Technologies used in intelligent warehousing.' Providing smart logistics insights according on example of 3 representative e- commerce corporations of the United States, China and Korea to other companies, which can be used by them during design of implementation of new smart logistics systems or improving of existing ones is the practical contribution of this research and it proposes future research directions, specifically improving technologies used in storage and intralogistics, optimizing last-mile delivery methods and developing contactless services for consumer convenience. This study provides academic implications by filling the research gap, as previous studies on trends in smart logistics were generally not focused on a specific industry, country, or company, resulting in extensive results.
author: 페도세에바 알리나

title: Understanding global research trends in the control and prevention of infectious diseases for children: Insights from text mining and topic modeling
abstract:
Abstract

Introduction

The emergence of novel infectious diseases has amplified the urgent need for effective prevention strategies, especially ones targeting vulnerable populations such as children. Factors such as the high incidence of both emerging and existing infectious diseases, delays in vaccinations, and routine exposure in communal settings heighten children's susceptibility to infections. Despite this pressing need, a comprehensive exploration of research trends in this domain remains lacking. This study aims to address this gap by employing text mining and modeling techniques to conduct a comprehensive analysis of the existing literature, thereby identifying emerging research trends in infectious disease prevention among children.

Methods

A cross‐sectional text mining approach was adopted, focusing on journal articles published between January 1, 2003, and August 31, 2022. These articles, related to infectious disease prevention in children, were sourced from databases such as PubMed, CINAHL, MEDLINE (Ovid), Scopus, and Korean RISS. The data underwent preprocessing using the Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK) in Python, with a semantic network analysis and topic modeling conducted using R software.

Results

The final dataset comprised 509 journal articles extracted from multiple databases. The study began with a word frequency analysis to pinpoint relevant themes, subsequently visualized through a word cloud. Dominant terms encompassed “vaccination,” “adolescent,” “infant,” “parent,” “family,” “school,” “country,” “household,” “community,” “HIV,” “HPV,” “COVID‐19,” “influenza,” and “diarrhea.” The semantic analysis identified “age” as a key term across infection, control, and intervention discussions. Notably, the relationship between “hand” and “handwashing” was prominent, especially in educational contexts linked with “school” and “absence.” Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling further delineated seven topics related to infectious disease prevention for children, encompassing (1) educational programs, (2) vaccination efforts, (3) family‐level responses, (4) care for immunocompromised individuals, (5) country‐specific responses, (6) school‐based strategies, and (7) persistent threats from established infectious diseases.

Conclusion

The study emphasizes the indispensable role of personalized interventions tailored for various child demographics, highlighting the pivotal contributions of both parental guidance and school participation.

Clinical Relevance

The study provides insights into the complex public health challenges associated with preventing and managing infectious diseases in children. The insights derived could inform the formulation of evidence‐based public health policies, steering practical interventions and fostering interdisciplinary synergy for holistic prevention strategies.
author: Oh, Won‐Oak;Lee, Eunji;Heo, Yoo‐jin;Jung, Myung‐Jin;Han, Jihee;

title: COVID-19 범유행 속 소셜 미디어를 통한 여론 및 우울감 표출 텍스트의 분석
abstract: 장기화된 COVID-19의 범유행은 전 세계적인 경제 규모의 축소는 물론 사회적 거리두기와 격리, 감염과 사망에 대한 두려움, 직접적인 감염 경험 등에 의한 고립감과 소외감, 정서적인 불안정, 심리적 외상 등의 다양한 문제 또한 촉발시켰다. 이에 따라 다양한 COVID-19 관련 문제 분석 연구가 등장했으나 의학적∙경제적 측면에서 접근한 연구가 대부분이었고, 일반 대중의 정서적 상황과 관심 주제에 대해 집중적으로 탐구한 연구는 부족한 실정이다. 유사한 연구들은 대부분 특정 국가 및 지역의 데이터만을 사용하였기에 분석 결과를 일반적으로 적용하기에는 지역적 한계가 존재하였고 그밖에는 단일한 분석 기법만을 적용하였기 때문에 단면적인 분석에 국한되는 경우가 많았다. 이에 본 연구는 다국적 이용자가 이용하는 소셜 미디어인 레딧(Reddit) 내의 COVID-19 관련 주제 게시판의 텍스트를 분석하여 전반적인 대중의 텍스트적 특성을 알아보고, 나아가 우울감을 표출하는 대중들의 텍스트적 특성 또한 밝히고자 하였다.&#xD; 본 연구는 ‘COVID 19’를 검색어로 사용하여 연관성(relevance) 기준 상위 14개의 COVID-19 관련 게시판(Subreddit)에서 2020년 1월부터 2021년 2월의 기간 중 가장 많은 추천을 받은 게시글과 댓글 내의 텍스트 데이터를 수집했으며, 추가적으로 부족한 2020년 1월의 데이터를 보충하기 위해 ‘COVID19’ 혹은 ‘Corona virus’ 라는 표현이 문장에 포함된 게시글을 수집하여 분석에 사용하였다. 이후 COVID-19와 관련하여 소셜 미디어를 통해 대중들의 텍스트적 특성을 알아보기 위해 DMR 토픽모델링, 이모지 빈도분석과 월별 감성분석을 실시하였다. 또한 그 중에서 우울감을 표출하는 문장을 추출하여 해당 데이터를 대상으로 LDA 토픽모델링, 이모지 빈도분석, 월별 감성분석과 개체명 인식 분석을 수행하였다.&#xD; 연구 결과로 우선, COVID-19 범유행과 관련한 대중들의 주요 관심 주제를 발견할 수 있었다. 대중들은 ‘마스크 착용’, ‘COVID-19 증상’, ‘봉쇄령’, ‘공동체’, ‘발생 현황 보도’의 5개 주제에 대해 관심을 가지고 있었으며, 이러한 관심 주제의 부상은 해당 시기의 사회적 이슈 및 COVID-19의 유행 정도와 유의미한 연관성을 가지고 있었다. 또한 COVID-19 범유행과 대중의 감성 사이의 연결 관계를 살펴본 결과, 범유행 초기의 대중의 평균 유인가는 빠른 COVID-19 유행의 영향으로 부정적인 정서가 만연하였으나 범유행이 장기화됨에 따라 대중의 유인가는 점차 긍정적인 정서의 범주로 완화되었고 이를 통해 COVID-19 범유행과 대중의 감성의 연결 관계가 비교적 느슨해진 것을 알 수 있었다. 마지막으로 COVID-19 범유행과 관련하여 우울감을 표출하는 대중들의 텍스트를 분석한 결과, 이들은 ‘일상적 불안’과 ‘COVID-19 증상’의 주제에 주된 관심을 보였으며 범유행의 초기에 가장 낮은 유인가를 기록하며 강한 부정적 감성을 나타냈다. 이후에도 다소 완화되었으나 여전히 큰 기복 없이 부정적 감성의 범주에 속하는 평균 유인가를 보였다. 또한 개체명 인식 분석을 통해 증상, 치료, 질병, 약물의 개체명 종류의 순서로 자주 언급함을 알 수 있었고, 개체명 기반 네트워크 분석으로 치료법, 신체적 증상 그리고 감정적 증상과 관련된 세 개의 하위 네트워크와 ‘불안’, ‘증상’, ‘슬픔’, ‘비사교적’, ‘의사’ 등의 구체적인 노드들이 네트워크에서 중심적 역할을 수행함을 확인했다. &#xD; 본 연구는 대규모의 데이터를 수집하여 범유행 시작 이후 1년 동안의 시간의 흐름에 따라 데이터를 분석하였기에 더 크고 다양한 표본을 통해 장기적인 텍스트 특성의 경향과 흐름을 관찰할 수 있었다. 또한 COVID-19의 범유행과 관련하여 보편적으로 적용 가능한 해석을 도출하였고 다양한 텍스트 마이닝 기법은 물론 딥러닝 기반의 개체명 인식 분석과 같은 다양한 접근 방식을 통해 다각도로 텍스트의 특성에 대해 분석했다는 점에 있어서 의의를 가진다.
author: 박혜린

title: Nussbaum의 역량 접근법에 근거한 국내외 교육 공적개발원조 연구 동향 비교 분석
abstract: 본 연구는 교육 공적개발원조(Official Development Assistance; ODA)와 관련한 국내외 연구 문헌을 대상으로 토픽모델링을 실행하여 국내외 연구를 비교 분석함으로써 교육ODA 연구 동향을 파악하고, 향후 교육ODA 관련 연구를 위한 시사점을 제공하기 위하여 실시되었다.&#xD; 국내외 교육ODA의 연구동향을 파악하기 위해 우리나라가 OECD/DAC 회원국에 가입한 2009년부터 2020년까지 발행된 학술 논문의 영문 초록을 수집하였으며, 국내 208편, 국외 213편의 논문이 분석에 활용되었다. 수집된 영문 초록을 바탕으로 상위 빈도 키워드와 상위 TF-IDF(Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency; 역문서빈도) 단어를 추출하였으며, Python3.9의 gensim 패키지를 활용하여 국내외 각각 15개의 토픽을 도출하고, Nussbaum의 역량이론에 근거하여 분류 한 후, 전체 연구 기간을 3개의 구간으로 나누어 토픽들에 대한 추세분석을 시행하였다. &#xD; 논의된 연구결과는 다음과 같다. 첫째, 국내 상위 빈도 단어는 training(147회), policy(117회), government(98회), country(92회), assistance(80회)로 나타났으며, 국외 상위 빈도의 단어는 policy(88회), university(86회), training(80회), assistance(70회), school(64회)로 나타났다. TF-IDF의 경우 국내는 training(10.84615), policy(9.807129), country(8.044422), government(7.654336), school(6.128423) 순서로 관련 연구에서 중요하게 사용되고 있었으며, 국외에서는 policy(8.759756), unive rsity(7.463235), training(6.611495), China(6.568474), school(5.917034)이 차례로 중요하게 활용되었다.&#xD; 둘째, 토픽모델링의 LDA 알고리즘 수행 결과 국내에서는 교사교육, 직업교육, 기술교육, 인권, 교육정책, 고등교육 등과 관련한 15개의 토픽이 도출되었다. 국외의 경우 교육 체제, 교육 환경, 교육재정, 능력 개발, 학습자, 원격교육, 의학 교육 등과 관련한 15개의 토픽이 정해졌다. &#xD; 셋째, 도출된 토픽을 바탕으로 전체 2009년부터 2020년의 기간을 4년씩 3구간으로 나누어 추세분석을 시행한 결과, 국내에서는 2009년부터 2010년대 초반까지 주로 정책과 국제 사례를 중심으로 연구되어 오다 구체적인 프로그램 적용과 관련된 연구들이 점차 실시되었다. 국외의 경우 3구간으로 시간이 흐르며 점차 연구 문헌 수가 증가했고 이는 교육ODA에 대한 국제적 관심이 높아지고 있다는 것을 나타낸다.&#xD; 본 연구결과에 따른 연구의 한계와 후속 연구를 위한 제언은 다음과 같다. 첫째, 본 연구에서는 토픽모델링을 위하여 교육ODA와 관련한 학술지 연구 논문만이 선정되었다. 그러나 국내외 교육ODA와 관련한 연구의 경우 다양한 국제기구와 교육기관에서 관련 연구를 활발하게 수행하였다. 따라서 연구보고서를 분석 대상으로 포함한다면 보다 많은 수의 데이터로 명확한 토픽 구분이 가능할 것이다. 둘째, 토픽모델링을 수행하기 위해 우리나라가 OECD/DAC 회원국에 가입한 2009년부터 2020년까지의 논문을 수집하였다. 그러나 국외의 경우 2009년 이전부터 활발하게 ODA 분야에 관한 연구가 진행되었을 가능성이 크기 때문에 문헌 수집의 범위를 더 넓혀 분석해볼 필요가 있다. 셋째, 향후 연구에서는 MDGs, SDGs와 같은 국제적으로 주요한 사건이 이루어진 시기를 중심으로 심층적인 연구 분석을 시행한다면 더 의미 있는 결과를 얻을 수 있을 것이다. 넷째, 본 연구에서는 LDA 알고리즘만이 연구 동향을 파악하는 데 활용되었는데, LDA는 토픽의 위계적인 성격을 나타내주지 않는다는 한계가 있다. 따라서 후속연구에서 도출된 키워드 간의 관계를 설명하는 네트워크 분석을 추가로 분석한다면 주제와 핵심어 간의 연결 관계를 더욱 면밀하게 확인할 수 있을 것이다.
author: 오여진

title: Systematic Literature Review (SLR): Explorations flood systems theory and appropriate modeling
abstract: <jats:p>Urban flood risk assessment conducts a comprehensive evaluation of hazard formative factors, hazard formative environment, hazard-affected bodies, and capabilities for disaster prevention and reduction in order to obtain an accurate assessment of flood risk levels. The current study aimed to conduct a systematic review of the existing literature on engagement outcomes, focusing on high-quality studies Each step of the SLR method and their results are explained in detail in the following subsections using SLR performed. Using the SLR method can help answer the objectives of this research in the form of: What type of modeling to overcome flooding This research uses the SLR method which aims to recognize, review, and evaluate Using bibliometric analysis.To achieve the goal of SLR, the variables of interest are organized based on the general characteristics of the article and the specific parameters used general  information about the article includes year of publication, type of analysis (quantitative, qualitative, cartographic or mixed), type and scale of  research, and the country or region where the research was conducted. The model consists of three components, including rainfall runoff, river channels, and flooding The flow in the channel was generated with a 1D diffusion wave model, and the outflow on the slope was generated with a 2D model.This article showed the basic steps that need to be followed to conduct SLR This method generates topic-specific existing knowledge, trends, and observed gaps and helps to draw relevant conclusions for policy makers and the scientific community. and the appropriate modeling is Press RRI refers to 2D grid-based fluid dynamics and is a model that combines a hydrological model and a flood model.</jats:p>
author: Brenda Arham;Muhamad Dimyati;

title: 감정 딥러닝 필터를 활용한 토픽 모델링 방법론
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to propose a methodology to derive positive keywords and negative keywords through deep learning to classify reviews into positive reviews and negative ones, and then refine the results of topic modeling using these keywords. Design/methodology/approach In this study, we extracted topic keywords by performing LDA-based topic modeling. At the same time, we performed attention-based deep learning to identify positive and negative keywords. Finally, we refined the topic keywords using these keywords as filters. Findings We collected and analyzed about 6,000 English reviews of Gyeongbokgung, a representative tourist attraction in Korea, from Tripadvisor, a representative travel site. Experimental results show that the proposed methodology properly identifies positive and negative keywords describing major topics.
author: 최병설;김남규;

title: Deep-Learning-based Cryptanalysis through Topic Modeling
abstract: Neural cryptography is a technique that uses neural networks for secure data encryption. Cryptoanalysis, on the other hand, deals with analyzing and decrypting ciphers, codes, and encrypted text without using a real key. Chosen-plaintext cryptanalysis is a subfield of cryptanalysis where both plain text and ciphertext are available and the goal is either to find the encryption technique, the encryption key, or both. This study addresses chosen plaintext cryptanalysis within public key cryptography, to categorize topics of encrypted text. Using a fixed encryption technique and key, the focus was placed on creating a framework that identifies the topic associated with ciphertext, using diverse plaintexts and their corresponding cipher texts. To our knowledge, this is the first time that chosen-plaintext cryptanalysis has been discussed in the context of topic modeling. The paper used deep learning techniques such as CNNs, GRUs, and LSTMs to process sequential data. The proposed framework achieved up to 67% precision, 99% recall, 80% F1-score, and 71% AUPR on a dataset, showcasing promising results and opening avenues for further research in this cryptanalysis subarea.
author: Kumar, Kishore;Tanwar, Sarvesh;Kumar, Shishir;

title: 딥러닝 및 토픽모델링 기법을 활용한 소셜 미디어의 자살 경향 문헌 판별 및 분석
abstract: 자살은 전 세계 사망 원인 중 4위이며 사회, 경제적 손실이 큰 난제이다. 본 연구는 자살 예방을 위하여 소셜미디어에 나타난 자살 관련 말뭉치를 구축하고 이를 통해 자살 경향 문헌을 분류할 수 있는 딥러닝 자동분류 모델을 만들고자 하였다. 또한, 자살 요인을 분석하기 위해 주제를 자동으로 추출하는 분석 기법인 토픽모델링을 활용하여 자살 관련 말뭉치를 세부 주제로 분류하고자 하였다. 이를 위해 소셜미디어 중 하나인 네이버 지식iN에 나타난 자살 관련 문헌 2,011개를 수집한 후 자살예방교육 매뉴얼을 기준으로 자살 경향 문헌 및 비경향 문헌 여부를 주석 처리하였으며, 이 데이터를 딥러닝 모델(LSTM, BERT, ELECTRA)로 학습시켜 자동분류 모델을 만들었다. 또한, 토픽모델링 기법의 하나인 LDA 기법으로 주제별 문헌을 분류하여 자살 요인을 발견하였고 이를 심층적으로 분석하기 위해 주제별로 동시출현 단어 분석 및 네트워크 시각화를 진행하였다.
author: 고영수;이주희;송민;

title: (A) hybrid approach for topic discovery and recommendations based on topic modeling and deep learning
author: Shafqat, Wafa

title: Adaptive Framework for Deep Learning Based Dynamic and Temporal Topic Modeling from Big Data
abstract:
Background:

The large amount of data emanated from social media platforms need scalable topic modeling in order to get current trends and themes of events discussed on such platforms. Topic modeling play crucial role in many natural language processing applications like sentiment analysis, recommendation systems, event tracking, summarization, etc.

Objective:

The aim of the proposed work is to adaptively extract the dynamically evolving topics over streaming data, and infer the current trends and get the notion of trend of topics over time. Because of various world level events, many uncorrelated streaming channels tend to start discussion on similar topics. We aim to find the effect of uncorrelated streaming channels on topic modeling when they tend to start discussion on similar topics.

Methods:

An adaptive framework for dynamic and temporal topic modeling using deep learning has been put forth in this paper. The framework approximates online latent semantic indexing constrained by regularization on streaming data using adaptive learning method. The framework is designed using deep layers of feedforward neural network.

Results:

This framework supports dynamic and temporal topic modeling. The proposed approach is scalable to large collection of data. We have performed exploratory data analysis and correspondence analysis on real world Twitter dataset. Results state that our approach works well to extract topic topics associated with a given hashtag. Given the query, the approach is able to extract both implicit and explicit topics associated with the terms mentioned in the query.

Conclusion:

The proposed approach is a suitable solution for performing topic modeling over Big Data. We are approximating the Latent Semantic Indexing model with regularization using deep learning with differentiable ℓ1 regularization, which makes the model work on streaming data adaptively at real-time. The model also supports the extraction of aspects from sentences based on interrelation of topics and thus, supports aspect modeling in aspect-based sentiment analysis.
author: Pathak, Ajeet R.;Pandey, Manjusha;Rautaray, Siddharth;

title: Deep Learning-based Sentiment Analysis and Topic Modeling on Tourism During Covid-19 Pandemic
abstract: The Covid-19 pandemic has disrupted the world economy and significantly influenced the tourism industry. Millions of people have shared their emotions, views, facts, and circumstances on numerous social media platforms, which has resulted in a massive flow of information. The high-density social media data has drawn many researchers to extract valuable information and understand the user’s emotions during the pandemic time. The research looks at the data collected from the micro-blogging site Twitter for the tourism sector, emphasizing sub-domains hospitality and healthcare. The sentiment of approximately 20,000 tweets have been calculated using Valence Aware Dictionary for Sentiment Reasoning (VADER) model. Furthermore, topic modeling was used to reveal certain hidden themes and determine the narrative and direction of the topics related to tourism healthcare, and hospitality. Topic modeling also helped us to identify inter-cluster similar terms and analyzing the flow of information from a group of a similar opinion. Finally, a cutting-edge deep learning classification model was used with different epoch sizes of the dataset to anticipate and classify the people’s feelings. The deep learning model has been tested with multiple parameters such as training set accuracy, test set accuracy, validation loss, validation accuracy, etc., and resulted in more than a 90% in training set accuracy tourism hospitality and healthcare reported 80.9 and 78.7% respectively on test set accuracy.
author: Mishra, Ram Krishn;Urolagin, Siddhaling;Jothi, J. Angel Arul;Neogi, Ashwin Sanjay;Nawaz, Nishad;

title: Topic modeling in short-text using non-negative matrix factorization based on deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Topic modeling for short texts is a challenging and interesting problem in the machine learning and knowledge discovery domains. Nowadays, millions of documents published on the internet from various sources. Internet websites are full of various topics and information, but there is a lot of similarity between topics, contents, and total quality of sources, which causes data repetition and gives the user the same information. Another issue is data sparsity and ambiguity because the length of the short text is limited, which causes unsatisfactory results and give irrelevant results to end-users. All these mentioned issues in short texts made an interesting topic for researchers to use machine learning and knowledge discovery techniques to discover underlying topics from a massive amount of data. In this paper, we propose a combination of deep reinforcement learning (RL) and semantics-assisted non-negative matrix factorization model to extract meaningful and underlying topics from short document contents. The main objective of this work is to reduce the problem of repetitive information and data sparsity in short texts to help the users to get meaningful and relevant contents. Furthermore, our propose model reviews an issue of the Seq2Seq approach based on the reinforcement learning perspective and provides a combination of reinforcement learning and SeaNMF formulation using the block coordinate descent algorithm. Moreover, we compare different real-world datasets by using numerical calculation and present a couple of state-of-art models to get better performance on short text document topic modeling. Based on experimental results and comparative analysis, our propose model outperforms the state of art techniques in terms of short document topic modeling.

title: Amenities and Rural Appalachia Economic Growth
abstract: Patterns of economic growth in rural Appalachia are examined with a focus on natural and built amenities. While the literature is clear that rural areas endowed with scenic beauty, lakes, forests, and wildlife, among other natural amenities, and coupled with built amenities such as golf courses, are experiencing robust economic growth. It is not clear if these patterns extend to rural Appalachia. In this applied research study we use data for rural U. S. counties. We estimate an augmented Carlino-Mills growth model with specific attention to growth patterns of Appalachia. We also build on the empirical modeling by adopting a Bayesian Modeling Average (BMA) approach to address the problem of model specification. We find that while there are some commonalities across the whole of the United States, the country is sufficiently heterogeneous that impact of amenities or other policy variables may be significantly different depending on where one is within the country. Our results suggest that while non-metropolitan Appalachia tends to follow national trends, there are sufficient differences that warrant special attention.

title: How Have Global Scientists Responded to Tackling COVID-19?
abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Since the outbreak of COVID-19, the global scientific communities across almost all countries have made urgent, intensive, and continuous effort on understanding, fighting and modeling the COVID-19 pandemic. COVID-19 research turns out to be the first overwhelming global scientific reaction to significant global crises and threats. This literature analysis report collects and summarizes the profiles, trends, quality and impact of this global scientific response. It collects and analyzes 346,267 scientific references in English, involving researchers from 189 countries and regions in 27 subject areas. The report generates a picture of how global scientists have responded to COVID-19 between Jan 2020 and Mar 2022 in terms of their publication quantity, impact, focused major problems, and research areas and methods over country/region, discipline and time and collaboratively. The report also captures broad-reaching distributions and trends of modeling COVID-19 by AI, data science, analytics, shallow and deep machine learning, epidemic modeling, applied mathematics, and social science methods, etc. We further show the correlations between publication quality and quantity and economic status and COVID-19 infections globally and in major countries and regions. The literature analysis results of this global scientific response to COVID-19 present a comprehensive global, regional and subject-specific picture of the significant cross-disciplinary, cross-country, cross-problem, and cross-technique profiles and differences of the COVID-19 publication quantity and quality. The report also discloses significant imbalances in the COVID-19 research across countries/regions, subject areas, problems, topics, methods, research collaborations, and economic statuses. title: Can global models provide insights into regional mitigation strategies? A diagnostic model comparison study of bioenergy in Brazil
abstract:
Abstract

The usefulness of global integrated assessment model (IAM) results for policy recommendation in specific regions has not been fully assessed to date. This study presents the variation in results across models for a given region, and what might be behind this variation and how model assumptions and structures drive results. Understanding what drives the differences across model results is important for national policy relevance of global scenarios. We focus on the use of bioenergy in Brazil, a country expected to play an important role in future bioenergy production. We use results of the Stanford University Energy Modeling Forum’s 33rd Study (EMF-33) model comparison exercise to compare and assess projections of Brazil’s bioenergy pathways under climate mitigation scenarios to explore how 10 global IAMs compare to recent trends in the country. We find that, in their current form, global IAMs have limited potential to supply robust insights into regional mitigation strategies. Our results suggest fertile ground for a new research agenda to improve regional representation in global IAMs with improved spatial and technological resolutions.

title: Fractional differencing in stock market price and online presence of global tourist corporations
abstract:
Purpose

This work aims to explore the behavior of stock market prices according to the autoregressive fractional differencing integrated moving average model. This behavior will be compared with a measure of online presence, search engine results as measured by Google Trends.

Design/methodology/approach

The study sample is comprised by the companies listed at the STOXX® Global 3000 Travel and Leisure. Google Finance and Yahoo Finance, along with Google Trends, were used, respectively, to obtain the data of stock prices and search results, for a period of five years (October 2012 to October 2017). To guarantee certain comparability between the two data sets, weekly observations were collected, with a total figure of 118 firms, two time series each (price and search results), around 61,000 observations.

Findings

Relationships between the two data sets are explored, with theoretical implications for the fields of economics, finance and management. Tourist corporations were analyzed owing to their growing economic impact. The estimations are initially consistent with long memory; so, they suggest that both stock market prices and online search trends deserve further exploration for modeling and forecasting. Significant differences owing to country and sector effects are also shown.

Originality/value

This research contributes in two different ways: it demonstrate the potential of a new tool for the analysis of relevant time series to monitor the behavior of firms and markets, and it suggests several theoretical pathways for further research in the specific topics of asymmetry of information and corporate transparency, proposing pertinent bridges between the two fields.
author: Flores-Muñoz, Francisco;Báez-García, Alberto Javier;Gutiérrez-Barroso, Josué

title: 중국 대학교 프로덕트 디자인학과 대학생들의 전문적 정체감이 온라인 학습체험에 미치는 영향에 관한 연구: 학업적 자기효능감과 온라인 학습참여도의 이중매개효과를 중심으로
abstract: 글로벌 혁신 추세와 중국 국내 산업 업그레이드의 시급한 요구에 부응 하기 위해 중국은 대학교 프로덕트 디자인 전문 분야에서 전례 없는 도전과 기회에 직면해 있다. 대학교 프로덕트 디자인 전공은 현대 사회의 고품질 디자인 인재에 대한 요구를 충족시키기 위해 학생들의 디자인 혁신 능력, 기술 응용 능력 및 시장 분석 능력을 배양하는 것을 목표로 하는 멀티 전공이라 할 수 있다. 이러한 맥락에서 프로덕트 디자인 교육을 심화시킬 필요가 있다. 이어서 대학교 프로덕트 디자인 전공 연구에 대한 투자와 지원을 늘리는 것은 교육의 질을 향상시킬 뿐만 아니라 새로운 경제 발전 추세에 적응하기 위한 불가피한 선택이기도 하다. 현대 교육 기술의 주요 혁신으로서 온라인 과정은 대학교 프로덕트 디자인을 전공하는 학생들에게 유연하고 편리한 학습 방법 을 제공한다. 온라인 과정 학습 경험은 많은 요인의 영향을 받는 대학 전문 인력 양성의 온라인 교육 효과를 측정하는 중요한 지표이기도 하다. 또한, 본 연구에서는 프로덕트 디자인 전공 학생들의 전문적 정체감과 온라인 수업 학습 체험과의 관계에서 학업 자아효능감과 온라인 참여도의 역할에 대해 고찰하였다. 본 논문에서는 전문적 정체감, 학업적 자기 효능감, 온라인 참여도, 온라인 수업 학습경험 척도를 이용하여 프로덕트 디자인 전공자를 대상으로 무작위로 사전조사를 실시하였다. 그런 다음 계층적 무작위 샘플링 원칙을 사용하여 중국의 전국 둥베이（系北） 지역, 화베이（牟北） 지역, 화둥（牟系） 지역, 화중（牟中） 지역, 화난（牟南） 지역 , 시난（西南） 지역 및 시베이（西北） 지역의 프로덕트 디자인 전공자를 대상 으로 데이터를 수집하였다. 통계 분석 소프트웨어 3？83,23를 사용하여 전처리 후, 유효한 데이터에 대해 프로덕트 디자인 전공자의 온라인 수업 학습 경험 의 인구통계학적 특성 차이를 분석하였다. 또 신뢰성과 타당성 분석 및 상관 분석을 수행했다. 다음으로 구조 방정식 모델링 도구인 새108.23을 사용하여 모형적합도 검증을 하였다. 마지막으로 경로분석 결과를 바탕으로 변수 간 인과관계를 검증하고, 전문적 정체감이 프로덕트 디자인 전공자의 온라인 수업 학습경험에 미치는 영향 을 검증하는 과정에서 학업적 자기효능감, 온라인 참여도의 매개효과 검증을 했다. 프로덕트 디자인학과 학생들의 온라인 수업 학습경험은 인구학적 변수 간 차별성 검증에 의하면 성별, 학년, 전형지원, 출신지, 재학학교 소재지, 학습방법 선호도 및 온라인 학습 참여 경험 프로덕트 디자인학과 학생들의 온라인 수업 학습경험 수준에 유의한 차이가 있었다. 연구에 따르면 남학생의 온라인 수업 학습 체험 수준은 여학생보다 현저히 높고, 수업 환경 체험과 학습 효과 인식의 두 가지 측면에서 남학생도 여학생 보다 현저히 높으며, 그중 저학년 학생（특히 대학교 2학년 학생）은 고학 년 학생（대학교 3학년 및 4학년 학생）보다 온라인 수업 체험감이 더 좋 게 나타났다. 프로덕트 디자인 전공 1차 전형 지원 학생은 온라인 수업 체험 및 각 차원에서 체험감이 더 좋게 나타났다. 시골출신 프로덕트 디자인 전공 학생들은 온라인 수업 학습 경험과 다양한 차원의 인식 수준에서 도시출신 학생들보다 현저히 낮게 나타났다. 학교의 소재지 역시 중요한 영향을 미치며, 프로덕트 디자인 전공 학생들은 온라인 수업의 학습 및 경험에서 화난（牟南） 지역과 시난（西南） 지역의 수준이 높은 반 면 둥베이（系北） 지역과 화베이（牟北） 지역의 수준은 낮은 것으로 나타났다. 오프라인학습과 온라인 오프라인 혼합 수업을 선호하는 프로덕트 디자인전공 학생들의 온라인 수업 학습 경험은 라이브 수업과 녹화수업보다 낮게 나타났다. 프로덕트 디자인학과 4학기를 거친 학생들은 1학기, 2학기, 3학기 과정을 거치는 것 보다 온라인 수업 학습 경험이 더 많았다. 본 연구에서는 온라인 수업 학습 체험에 대한 전공정체감의 직접적인 영향과 학업적 자기효능감, 온라인 참여도가 전공 정체감과 온라인 수업 학습 체험 간의 간접적인 영향을 중점적으로 살펴보았다. 상관관계 결과 제품디자인 전공자의 전공정체감과 학업적 자기효능감, 학업적 자기효능 감과 온라인 수업 학습경험 사이에는 강한 양의 상관관계가 있는 것으로 나타났다. 동시에 전문적인 인식과 온라인 참여에 있어서, 온라인 참여와 온라인 강의 학습 경험 사이에는 양의 상관 관계가 있다는 것으로 나타 났다. 가설 검증의 결과에서 알 수 있듯이, 전문적 정체감이 대학 제품 디자인을 전공하는 학생들의 온라인 과정 학습 및 경험에 상당한 긍정적 인 예측 효과가 있음을 보여주었다. 또한, 전문적 정체감은 학업적 자기효능감과 온라인 참여도를 긍정적 으로 예측할 수 있으며, 학업적 자기효능감과 온라인 참여도는 전문적 정체감과 온라인 수업 학습체험 사이에서 매개역할을 하는 것으로 확인 되었으며, 학업적 자기효능감은 전문적 정체감과 온라인 수업 학습체험 수준 사이에서 매개효과가 전체 효과량에서 유의한 비중을 차지하였다. 또한, 프로덕트 디자인 전공자 중 학업적 자기효능감도 온라인 참여도에 긍정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있음을 예측할 수 있다. 따라서 학업적 자기효 능감과 온라인 참여도가 전문적 정체감과 온라인 수업 학습체험 사이에 연쇄적인 중개효과를 만들어냄으로써 '전문적 정체감- 학업적 자기효능 감-온라인참여도- 온라인 수업 학습체험’의 영향경로를 형성하고 있다. 본 연구에서는 전문적 정체감, 학업적 자기효능감, 온라인 참여도, 온 라인 수업 학습경험과의 관계를 바탕으로 전문적 정체감, 학업적 자기효 능감, 온라인 참여도 향상을 통한 대학 프로덕트 디자인 전공자의 온라 인 수업 학습경험 향상을 위한 구체적인 방안을 제시하였다. 구체적인 조치는 다음과 같다. 온라인 수업 콘텐츠의 상호 작용 및 실천 강화, 적극적인 온라인 학습 커뮤니티 구축, 수업 콘텐츠 및 구조 최적화이다. 실습 및 응용 중심의 학습 경 험을 강화하고 전문적 정체감의 자기 반성을 촉진하며 직업 계획 및 개발 지도를 제공한다. 목표 또는 작업을 세분화 하고 목표의 실현 가능성과 명확성을 설정한다. 대화형 학습자료 제공, 팀 프로젝트를 통한 학생들의 협동학습 장려, 포럼 및 토론장 운영, 동반 자 평가 메커니즘 구현, 가상 커뮤니티 및 네트워크 구축, 게임화 학습 구축 등이다.
author: LIU FUYING

title: 국채 Term Spread와 거시경제요인의 국가간 실증 분석 : - 중·미·한 시장 비교 연구 -
abstract: 본 연구는 국채 Term Spread가 거시경제를 예측하는 선행지표로 주목받고 있는 배경에서, 중국·미국·한국 3개국을 비교하여 그 결정 요인과 영향 경로를 실증적으로 분석하였다. 선진국인 미국의 사례에서는 Term Spread가 경기 침체를 예고하는 신호로 활용되었으나, 신흥국이나 개방도가 다른 경제에서는 그 의미와 작동 메커니즘에 차이가 있을 수 있다. 이에 본 연구는 경제구조와 금융시장 특성이 상이한 중국, 미국, 한국을 대상으로 Term Spread의 거시경제 예측력과 국가 간 이질성을 규명하였다.&#xD; 연구 방법으로 벡터 자기회귀(VAR) 모형과 GARCH 모형 등 계량경제 분석기법을 적용하였으며 산업생산지수, 소비자물가지수(CPI), 정책금리(CHIBOR, 연방기금금리, 콜금리), 실효환율 등 주요 거시경제 변수를 활용하였다. 또한 광의의통화(M2), 자본 이동, 정책 불확실성 등의 변수를 포함하여 Term Spread와 거시 변수 간의 동태적 관계와 변동성을 다각적으로 검증하였다.&#xD; 실증분석 결과, 이따르면 첫째, 세 국가 모두에서 통화정책이 Term Spread 변동의 핵심적인 영향 요인으로 나타났다. 특히 중국은 정책금리 변화에 대한 Term Spread의 민감도가 높았고, 미국은 통화정책 신호가 장기금리 기대에 점진적으로 반영되는 '기대 앵커링 효과'가 뚜렷했다. 한국은 높은 자본계정 개방도로 인해 미국 통화정책의 외부 파급효과가 국내 통화정책 효과를 일부 상쇄하는 경향을 보였다.&#xD; 둘째, 경제성장 및 인플레이션의 영향력이 국가별로 상이하게 나타났다. 경제성장과 Term Spread의 양(+)의 상관관계는 미국에서 직접적으로 확인된 반면, 중국과 한국에서는 간접적 경로(물가 및 신용 경로)를 통해 나타났다. 인플레이션과 Term Spread 간의 예상된 음(-)의 관계는 세 국가 모두에서 기각되었으며, 오히려 인플레이션 상승 시 Term Spread가 확대되는 현상이 관찰되었다. 이는 인플레이션 기대 변화가 단기 정책금리 대응보다 장기금리 결정에 더 큰 영향을 미쳤기 때문이다.&#xD; 셋째, 환율 변동과 자본 흐름 등 대외 충격 요인의 영향은 국가별로 다르게 나타났다. 한국은 환율 약세 시 Term Spread가 확대되는 반면, 미국은 달러화의 기축통화 지위로 위기 시 자본유입이 장기금리를 낮추어 Term Spread를 축소시켰다. 중국은 자본규제로 인해 대외 충격의 영향이 제한적이었다.&#xD; 마지막으로, 정책 불확실성 증대가 Term Spread 변동성에 영향을 미치는 관계가 일부 확인되었으나, 데이터 제한으로 직접적 측정이 어려웠다. 향후 연구에서는 정책 불확실성 지표(EPU)를 보다 정교하게 계량화하여 분석할 필요가 있다.&#xD; 이러한 실증 결과는 국채 Term Spread가 거시경제 및 통화정책의 상호작용을 반영하는 유용한 지표이며, 각국의 경제구조와 금융시장 환경을 고려한 맞춤형 정책 수립의 중요성을 시사한다.
author: 싱루이쿤

title: The Fintech Revolution and Its Impact on Small Businesses in the U.S | The Fintech Revolution and Its Impact on Small Businesses in the U.S.
abstract: The Fintech Revolution and Its Impact on Small Businesses in the U.S.  Abstract  Fintechs have profoundly transformed the American financial sector, creating new opportunities for small entrepreneurs and reshaping how banking services are devised, offered, and used. This article analyzes the role of fintechs in the United States, focusing on their influence on digital payments, embedded finance, neobanks, and other emerging financial services. It also compares the U.S. landscape with Brazil's, highlighting similarities, differences, and trends that may shape the future of both countries’ financial ecosystems. Drawing on market analysis and case studies, the discussion shows how small businesses can benefit from more accessible and customized solutions, and how this new reality demands regulatory, educational, and technological adaptations to ensure sustainable sector growth. Finally, the article evaluates the impact of these transformations on financial inclusion and economic dynamism, especially for smaller entrepreneurs.    1. Introduction  The financial sector has traditionally been considered a high-barrier environment dominated by large banks and established institutions. However, the emergence of fintechs—companies that blend cutting-edge technology with financial services—has broken these monopolies, providing agile, accessible solutions tailored to the specific needs of different consumer and business profiles. This trend is especially prominent in the United States, where new startups receive billions of dollars in funding and grow at a rapid pace, revolutionizing payment methods, credit provision, financial management, and more.  For small businesses, this trend represents a chance to reinvent processes and increase the efficiency of financial management. In the past, entrepreneurs faced difficulties accessing loans at competitive rates or offering diverse payment methods to clients. Now, thanks to fintechs, these limitations can be overcome through digital platforms, real-time data analytics, and innovative business models.  This article delves into the fintech revolution in the U.S. and its influence on the ecosystem of micro and small enterprises, while also comparing the North American context with that of Brazil. We discuss trends such as digital payments, embedded finance, and neobanks, assessing both the opportunities and challenges of this disruptive landscape. Finally, we analyze the role of entrepreneurs in adopting these solutions and explore future prospects for the sector.    2. The Fintech Landscape in the U.S.  2.1 Growth and Diversity  The American fintech ecosystem is among the most dynamic worldwide, encompassing thousands of startups offering services in areas like payments, credit, insurance, investments, and financial management. Several factors drive this growth, including the availability of venture capital, a culture of innovation, and a large consumer market adept at using technology.  Although many fintechs focus on the B2C segment—delivering services directly to end users—the presence of solutions aimed at small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) continues to rise. These businesses find crucial support in this new model for financial transactions, cash flow management, supplier payments, and even more flexible lines of credit.  2.2 Regulatory Environment and Government Support  In the United States, financial sector regulations are fragmented, involving both federal and state agencies. While this can create uncertainties, it also permits certain states to enact policies more favorable to innovation—resulting in a kind of regulatory competition to attract fintech entrepreneurs. The existence of regulatory sandboxes, where new solutions can be tested under official supervision, further spurs sector expansion.  2.3 Financial Inclusion  In a country of continental dimensions, the challenge of reaching underserved populations also creates avenues for fintechs committed to promoting financial inclusion. Small businesses located in rural areas, for example, may find in these solutions a way to accept digital payments or access microcredit, services previously out of reach.    3. Fintechs and Small Businesses: Opportunities and Challenges  3.1 Access to Credit and Financing Options  One of the greatest pain points for small businesses is the challenge of securing working capital. Traditional banks frequently require high collateral, extensive credit history, and cumbersome processes that delay the release of funds. Conversely, fintechs specializing in credit rely on algorithms and data analytics to dynamically assess risk, granting loans to previously marginalized groups. This new approach reduces dependence on conventional credit reviews, paving the way for entrepreneurs with limited financial track records but promising performance metrics.  3.2 Digital Payments and Market Expansion  In the post-pandemic setting, e-commerce growth and the adoption of contactless payment methods have become even more pronounced. Small businesses that embrace fintech-based digital payment solutions expand their reach and can compete with larger contenders, attracting customers from different regions across the country. Moreover, transaction fees often run lower than those charged by major card acquirers, leading to notable savings.  3.3 Integrated Financial Management  Several fintechs offer platforms that bring together multiple services in a single environment—invoice issuance, accounts payable and receivable tracking, and sales data analysis, for example. This saves the entrepreneur time and affords a holistic view of the business, facilitating decision-making. On the other hand, small firms that resist these technologies risk falling behind more efficient competitors.  3.4 Challenges  Despite these advantages, hurdles remain. Regulatory issues, cybersecurity, and financial education must be addressed for SMEs to fully adopt fintech services. Lack of familiarity with digital platforms or fear of fraud can inhibit the uptake of services that, in principle, simplify financial operations.    4. Key Trends: Digital Payments, Embedded Finance, and Neobanks  4.1 Digital Payments  The exponential growth of e-commerce and the widespread use of mobile devices have fueled the development of numerous digital payment solutions. Small businesses can now process transactions via QR codes, digital wallets, and payment links, offering customers a more convenient experience. Such methods often have competitive fees and quicker settlement times, improving the merchant’s cash flow. Additionally, fintechs generate detailed reports on each sale, aiding business owners in understanding consumer behavior.  4.2 Embedded Finance  Embedded finance involves integrating financial services into platforms or apps that are not inherently banking-related. For instance, an inventory management tool might provide financing options for replenishing stock, or a meal-delivery platform could extend microloans to restaurants needing a working capital boost. This trend renders financial services more accessible and context-specific, easing day-to-day business activities for small companies and minimizing red tape. Fintechs that invest in partnerships with businesses in other industries can broaden their market presence and tailor solutions to specialized needs.  4.3 Neobanks and Digital Banking Models  Neobanks—financial institutions operating exclusively online with no physical branches—represent a major segment of the U.S. fintech ecosystem. They cater to both individuals and businesses, offering checking accounts, debit and credit cards, and expense-management tools. For small entrepreneurs, these platforms are agile and cost-effective, typically featuring lower fee packages and intuitive procedures for account setup.  Neobanks may also provide features like multiple subaccounts for specific uses (tax reserves, payroll, or working capital) and integrate with accounting software. The simplicity and transparency of these offerings draw micro and small businesses seeking a smoother, more customized banking experience.  4.4 Decentralization and New Financing Methods  Meanwhile, crowdfunding and peer-to-peer lending have seen increased demand, permitting retail investors to lend directly to businesses. While not strictly part of the neobank concept, such innovations reinforce the decentralized nature of finance, enabling small businesses to obtain credit without resorting to conventional banks. Even though these platforms face regulatory hurdles, they highlight the wide range of financial alternatives emerging from the fintech boom.    5. Comparing the U.S. and Brazilian Scenarios  5.1 Similarities  Both the United States and Brazil have rapidly expanding fintech sectors, albeit at different stages of maturity. As in the U.S., Brazilian fintechs stand out by delivering services that are generally more affordable than those of large banks. In both countries, small businesses struggle with accessing credit and seeking low-cost, efficient payment methods. Hence, digital payment solutions and alternative credit platforms have achieved considerable popularity.  In both contexts, the proliferation of smartphones and internet connectivity has spurred the adoption of digital wallets and finance management apps. The availability of APIs and cloud-based technologies has also streamlined system integrations and fueled partnerships between fintechs and other industries.  5.2 Differences  Nevertheless, notable differences persist. Brazil’s regulatory landscape is more centralized, with the Central Bank taking a leading role in pushing digitization and competition policies, including PIX and Open Banking initiatives. Meanwhile, in the U.S., the patchwork of federal and state rules produces varied challenges and opportunities. Another distinction is that the U.S.’s larger capital markets allow for greater volumes of investment in fintech ventures.  In Brazil, financial inclusion is still a work in progress. Although a large part of the population has access to basic financial services, a considerable segment remains unbanked or underbanked, a reality that fosters demand for fintechs with inclusion-based missions. In contrast, while the U.S. has fewer unbanked individuals, fintechs place a stronger emphasis on customization and user experience.    6. The Role of Fintechs in Financial Inclusion and Entrepreneurship  For small entrepreneurs, financial inclusion goes beyond simply owning a bank account. It encompasses services that support planning, staff development, and growth in a sustainable manner. Fintechs address these gaps by offering credit based on alternative data analytics, round-the-clock digital customer support, and integration with business management tools.  In rural areas or low-income communities across the U.S., many emerging businesses benefit from such solutions, avoiding the need to visit physical bank branches and paying lower fees for more personalized service. This environment fosters local entrepreneurship, stimulating job creation and economic growth.  It is also worth noting that some fintech companies partner with NGOs and government bodies to promote financial literacy and provide micro-loans to populations previously invisible to conventional banks. As a result, the ecosystem gains resilience and diversity, encouraging innovation in products and services tailored to those that were not traditional banking priorities.    7. Barriers and Risks  While the fintech revolution holds clear advantages for small businesses, significant challenges remain:      Complex Regulation: The lack of nationwide standards in the U.S. can create overlaps among different regulatory authorities, leading to uncertainty for fintech entrepreneurs and complicating expansion efforts across states.     Cybersecurity: Digital platforms are prime targets for attacks and fraud. Smaller businesses may be especially vulnerable if they do not implement adequate security protocols.     Financial Education Gap: Many entrepreneurs are unfamiliar with—or skeptical of—fintech services. This knowledge gap can slow the adoption of tools that could improve cash flow and enhance competitiveness.     Unequal Access: In regions with poor internet infrastructure or lower educational levels, digital solutions may have a diminished impact or require increased training.    Beyond these hurdles, there is the risk of market concentration, whereby a handful of large fintechs dominate the industry, effectively recreating an oligopoly similar to that seen in the traditional banking system. Achieving sustainable ecosystem growth thus demands a combination of regulatory incentives, corporate social responsibility, and ongoing investment in security and education.    8. Future Perspectives and Innovations  Recent trends suggest fintech’s growth trajectory is unlikely to slow, pointing toward several future developments:      Open Finance: Evolving from Open Banking to Open Finance will allow data sharing among multiple financial institutions and related sectors, facilitating highly customized products. Small businesses could benefit from greater control over where and how their data is stored and deployed.     Advanced AI and Predictive Modeling: As artificial intelligence algorithms grow more sophisticated, risk assessments and consumer behavior analyses will become increasingly refined. Loan disbursements and interest rates could be personalized, reducing default rates and expanding access to credit.     Blockchain and Smart Contracts: Although blockchain adoption remains relatively limited, its capacity for secure transactions, identity verification, and automated contract execution holds promise. For small businesses, this may streamline processes and reduce intermediary costs.     Integration with Other Sectors: Embedded finance is poised to extend into logistics, education, healthcare, and numerous other areas. Consequently, fintech solutions will likely become more ubiquitous, popping up within various platforms and apps.    Over the long term, these innovations are expected to boost competition and efficiency within the financial system. Small businesses will have a broader spectrum of tools to manage capital and promote sustainable growth. It falls to entrepreneurs to monitor these shifts and responsibly adopt the tools best suited to their operational needs.    9. Practical Recommendations for Small Entrepreneurs  To leverage opportunities offered by the fintech revolution, small entrepreneurs should consider these steps:      Research and Compare Services: Before committing to any platform, assess fees, functionalities, support channels, and market reputation. Not all solutions are compatible with every business model.     Financial Education: Invest in staff training to better understand data analysis, cash flow control, and risk management, thus maximizing the benefits of digital tools.     System Integration: Whenever possible, unify sales, inventory, payroll, and banking data onto interoperable platforms. This optimization provides greater financial visibility and efficiency.     Contingency Plans: Though fintechs offer speed and convenience, it is important to maintain emergency reserves and account for potential crises. This safeguards the business from excessive reliance on a single credit source.     Digital Security: Employ multi-factor authentication, data backups, and anti-malware solutions to protect against fraud and data breaches.    The fintech revolution involves not only technological transformation but also a cultural shift. Small entrepreneurs who understand this dynamic and manage their resources more deliberately stand a better chance of thriving amid the competitive landscape.    10. Conclusion  The fintech revolution in the United States not only reshapes the traditional financial landscape but also significantly impacts the development of small businesses, both domestically and in countries like Brazil. By enabling new ways of handling payments, credit, and financial management, fintechs are making the financial ecosystem more dynamic and inclusive, offering customized services that can bolster the growth of smaller enterprises.  Comparatively, Brazil follows similar trends, although its centralized regulatory approach and specific government initiatives have differently influenced the rise and expansion of fintechs. Even so, innovations in digital payments, embedded finance, and neobanks transcend national boundaries, fueled by an increasingly connected and demanding customer base.  On the other hand, this rapidly expanding sector faces challenges, such as the need for appropriate regulation, cybersecurity measures, financial education, and prevention of market concentration. The success of the ecosystem hinges on balancing competitiveness with social responsibility, ensuring that fintech benefits reach underserved communities.  In essence, the fintech revolution represents an irreversible shift in how money and credit are managed. For small businesses, this phenomenon offers the chance to break down historical barriers to financial services, drive innovation, and ultimately contribute to broader economic stability and prosperity.
